items.title: Explore Copilot vision GA: attach images and PDFs to chat
items.description: Copilot vision is now generally available. You can attach images (JPEG, PNG, GIF, WebP) and PDFs directly to Copilot Chat prompts so the model reasons about what it sees alongside your code. Available in VS Code, github.com, Visual Studio, and Copilot CLI. Useful for UI bug reports, architecture diagrams, and error screenshots in AI app development.

items.title: Explore Copilot enterprise managed-settings.json for AI governance
items.description: Enterprise managed-settings.json is now generally available for GitHub Enterprise Cloud. Admins define Copilot policies—allowed models, extensions, and governance rules—in a file in a .github-private repo. Policies propagate to all Copilot clients including VS Code, CLI, and the web. Key for customer conversations on enterprise AI standards and compliance.

items.title: Build a safe agent harness with file access and approval gates using Microsoft Agent Framework
items.description: Part 2 of the Agent Harness series: add a file-access provider (read/write CSV portfolio data), human approval gates for risky tool calls, and durable memory (in-session and cross-session) to an MAF agent. Demonstrates key safety and trust patterns for production agentic apps that read enterprise data and must gate consequential actions behind human approval.

items.title: Build long-running MCP server tools on Azure Functions
items.description: Tutorial covering how to build MCP tools that exceed the default client timeout using Azure Durable Functions or notification callbacks. Practical for AI app teams exposing enterprise operations as MCP tools on Azure Functions, where tool execution times can be unbounded (e.g. data pipelines, batch jobs, external API calls with retries).

items.title: Explore agentic Logic Apps for routing Azure Service Health alerts to service owners
items.description: Walkthrough showing how to build an agentic Logic Apps workflow that automatically routes Azure Service Health alerts to the correct service owner teams based on affected subscription, resource group, or service type. Demonstrates real-world agentic integration patterns for AI-enabled operations and enterprise incident management, directly applicable to customer reliability conversations.

items.title: Explore Agent Framework Orchestration Patterns 1.0 GA
items.description: Sequential, concurrent, group chat, handoff, and magentic orchestration patterns are now stable (1.0) in the Microsoft Agent Framework SDKs. You can pick the coordination pattern that best fits your use case without working around SDK maturity. Magentic is the most autonomous: give it a goal, a manager, and specialists and the manager decides how the team works. Review the patterns, build a small multi-agent demo using magentic orchestration, and understand when to use each pattern.

items.title: Explore Agent Skills for .NET — stable GA release
items.description: Agent Skills is now GA in the Microsoft Agent Framework for .NET. It is an open format for packaging domain expertise that agents discover and use on demand. Each skill has a SKILL.md metadata file, optional scripts, and reference documents. Agents load only what they need using a four-stage progressive disclosure pattern (advertise → load instructions → read resources → execute), keeping context windows lean. Build and register a custom skill, then wire it into an agent to see on-demand skill loading in action.

items.title: Explore the GitHub Copilot desktop app — now available to all plans
items.description: The GitHub Copilot standalone desktop app is now GA and available on every Copilot plan (including Free). It provides agent-driven development from the desktop without needing a browser or IDE plugin — sign in with your GitHub account and start autonomous coding sessions on macOS, Windows, or Linux. Download the app, run a real-world task end-to-end, and compare the agent session workflow to chat-in-IDE use.

items.title: Explore GitHub Copilot's .NET upgrade agent for application modernization
items.description: The GitHub Copilot app now includes a .NET upgrade agent that automates the full modernisation workflow: it assesses the application, evaluates dependencies, generates a structured upgrade plan, creates implementation tasks, and executes the work — handling build failures and dependency conflicts as they surface. This is highly relevant for teams managing legacy .NET Framework or .NET 6/7/8 applications. Try it against a real or sample project and review the generated upgrade plan and PRs.

items.title: Explore Microsoft Foundry June 2026 — agent publishing to M365 GA and Toolboxes
items.description: The June 2026 Microsoft Foundry release covers two major milestones: (1) Publishing Foundry agents directly into Microsoft 365 Copilot and Teams is now GA — agents support goal-driven execution, checkpoints, and human escalation natively inside Teams. (2) Toolboxes add new built-in skills including Browser Automation, Work IQ, Fabric IQ, and Tool Search, plus Routines for repeatable task sequences. Claude in Foundry also reached GA. Read the What's New digest, then build and publish a simple agent to Teams to validate the end-to-end flow.

items.title: Explore Agent Skills for Python in Microsoft Agent Framework (GA)
items.description: Agent Skills for Python is now stable and production-ready in Microsoft Agent Framework (July 15 2026). Skills are reusable bundles of domain expertise — instructions, reference documents, and scripts — that agents load only when a task requires them. Teams can author and ship skills independently then compose them into any agent. Complements the earlier .NET Skills GA. Build a skill and attach it to a Python agent to test the full authoring flow.

items.title: Lab: Agentic Autofix for GitHub Code Scanning Alerts (Public Preview)
items.description: GitHub Copilot Agentic Autofix entered public preview on July 10 2026 for all code scanning alerts (CodeQL and third-party). It works like a developer: explores relevant files, proposes a fix, reruns the original analysis to confirm the alert is closed, then opens a pull request. Enable it on a repository with code scanning, trigger an alert, and observe the full agentic remediation loop.

items.title: Explore MCP Enterprise Authorization with Microsoft Entra and Azure App Service
items.description: Published July 16 2026, this App Service team deep-dive covers how to add enterprise-grade authorization to MCP servers today using Microsoft Entra ID and App Service built-in auth. Covers Entra app registrations, OAuth scopes, and App Service Easy Auth to secure MCP tool endpoints without custom middleware. Essential reading for teams exposing agentic tools inside corporate boundaries.

items.title: Explore Agent Framework Declarative Workflows 1.0
items.description: Agent Framework Declarative Workflows 1.0 (GA, Jul 23 2026) lets you define multi-agent orchestration — step sequencing, branching, and handoffs — in YAML/config rather than application code. This decouples workflow logic from the agent runtime, making flows easier to version, test, and hand off. Critical for App Innovation engineers building production multi-agent systems on Azure.

items.title: Explore the Microsoft Agent Framework Harness (GA)
items.description: The Agent Framework Harness (GA, Jul 22 2026) is a batteries-included runtime for .NET and Python that collapses the full agent pipeline — function invocation, history persistence, compaction, approvals, web search, and telemetry — into a single call. Engineers supply instructions and tools; the harness handles the rest. Reduces boilerplate and makes production-grade agents dramatically faster to ship.

items.title: Explore GitHub MCP Server support for the next MCP specification
items.description: The MCP protocol transitions to a stateless model on July 28 2026, and the GitHub MCP Server already supports the new spec. The update includes official MCP conformance tests that AI-assisted tools can use to validate correctness. Understanding stateless MCP is essential for anyone building or integrating MCP servers and clients in Copilot Extensions or Azure AI agent toolchains.

items.title: Explore Agent Automation Controls in GitHub Issues (Public Preview)
items.description: GitHub Issues now exposes rationale, confidence scores, and an approvals flow for agent-driven label, type, assign, and close operations (public preview, Jul 23 2026). Engineers can configure whether automations apply directly or suggest changes for human review. Understanding these governance controls is important for responsible agentic CI/CD pipelines and issue-triage workflows.

items.title: Explore Copilot Cloud Agent for Linear — Generally Available
items.description: Copilot cloud agent for Linear is now GA (Jul 23 2026). Assigning a Linear issue to Copilot triggers an autonomous loop: it creates a branch, writes and tests code, and opens a PR, with controls to pause, redirect, or restrict the agent from within Linear. Studying this end-to-end agentic coding workflow illustrates patterns applicable to any Copilot cloud agent integration with project management tooling.

items.title: Explore MCP C# SDK v2.0 — stateless HTTP and Multi Round-Trip Requests
items.description: The MCP C# SDK reached v2.0 implementing the 2026-07-28 revision of the MCP specification — the largest protocol revision since launch. Key changes: HTTP is now stateless by default (no session handshake), the HTTP surface is standardised so ordinary load balancers can route MCP traffic, and Multi Round-Trip Requests enable interactive tools without long-lived sessions. Backward-compatible with v1 code. Directly relevant for building MCP servers on ASP.NET Core.

items.title: Explore Copilot Code Review with Agent Skills and MCP (GA)
items.description: Copilot code review support for agent skills and MCP servers is now generally available for all Copilot Pro, Pro+, Business, and Enterprise plans. Agent skills (via SKILL.md files in .github/skills) let you embed team-specific coding standards into every review. MCP server connections pull context from issue trackers, documentation systems, and service catalogs directly into the review. Attribution on skill/MCP comments is also new. A direct productivity multiplier for PR workflows.

items.title: Explore GitHub Copilot in VS Code July 2026 — Vision GA and Multi-Chat Sessions
items.description: VS Code v1.127–v1.131 (July 2026) shipped several notable features: Copilot Vision (paste images and PDFs into chat) is now generally available; multi-chat sessions let you fork and compare approaches within one agent session; worktrees support lets each agent session work in an isolated Git worktree; and subagent tracking shows model, elapsed time, and active tool per running subagent. High daily-workflow impact for agentic development.

items.title: Explore Agent Framework: composing multi-agent systems with GitHub Copilot SDK and Squad
items.description: Microsoft Agent Framework (MAF) v1.0 now has a first-party adapter for the GitHub Copilot SDK, enabling you to wire a coding-capable Copilot agent into a MAF IServiceCollection alongside other agents. The blog post also introduces Squad — an open-source multi-agent framework (aka.ms/copilot-squad) where a coordinator dispatches tasks to specialist agents. The combination provides agent runtime, model abstraction, telemetry, and coding capability in one .NET app.

items.title: Explore dynamic Agent Skill discovery from MCP servers in .NET
items.description: Microsoft.Agents.AI.Mcp (released this week for .NET) lets agents discover and load Agent Skills on demand from an MCP server rather than bundling them at build time. The server advertises skills via a skill://index.json discovery document; agents pull full instructions only when a task matches. This enables centralised skill governance — domain experts publish once, all agents across the organisation pick up updates without redeployment.

items.title: Trigger Copilot cloud agent automations with issue and PR comments
items.description: GitHub Copilot cloud agent now supports automations triggered by issue or pull request comments. Engineers can set up workflows that auto-generate documentation, triage bugs, or run custom tasks simply by posting a comment. This unlocks comment-driven AI pipelines directly in GitHub, reducing context-switching and enabling richer agentic patterns in everyday developer workflows.

items.title: Customize reasoning level for GitHub Copilot cloud agent tasks
items.description: When delegating tasks to the Copilot cloud agent, engineers can now select the reasoning level for models that support it. Higher reasoning levels improve quality on complex refactors and architecture tasks; lower levels speed up simpler changes. Understanding how to tune this setting is key to getting the best cost-to-quality ratio from agentic coding workflows.

items.title: Explore Markdown for Agents in Azure App Service (public preview)
items.description: Azure App Service now supports a Markdown-for-Agents capability in public preview, letting hosted AI agents render structured Markdown responses directly through the platform runtime. This simplifies surfacing rich agent output in web and Teams surfaces without custom rendering logic. Lab the preview to understand how it integrates with existing App Service-hosted agent endpoints.

items.title: Built-in observability for serverless AI agents on Azure Functions
items.description: Azure Functions now ships built-in observability tooling for serverless AI agents, providing traces, logs, and metrics without requiring manual instrumentation. For App Innovation engineers building event-driven agent handlers, this removes a significant operational gap and aligns Functions-based agents with the observability story in Container Apps and App Service.

items.title: Use connectors with Managed Identity in Logic Apps Standard extension
items.description: Logic Apps Standard now supports authenticating built-in connectors with Managed Identity directly from the VS Code extension, eliminating the need to store connection strings or client secrets in app settings. This is a significant security improvement for enterprise integration workflows and aligns with zero-trust best practices for secret-free deployments.

items.title: Explore GitHub Copilot Agent Plugins 1.0
items.description: Agent Plugins 1.0 reached GA across VS Code, the Copilot CLI, and the Copilot app on 2026-08-12. Build a plugin once and deploy it to any compatible agent client. This is a fundamental extensibility milestone for teams authoring custom Copilot behaviours and agentic workflows. Study the plugin manifest schema, tool declarations, and distribution model.

items.title: Explore Azure Container Apps Sandboxes (Preview)
items.description: Azure Container Apps Sandboxes entered public preview on 2026-08-11. Sandboxes provide isolated, ephemeral execution environments for AI agent workloads, preventing cross-tenant contamination and reducing blast radius for untrusted code execution. Key for building secure multi-tenant AI apps. Study the sandbox lifecycle, resource limits, and integration with Dapr and KEDA.

items.title: Explore Microsoft.Extensions.AI Routing and Failover
items.description: The .NET blog announced experimental routing and failover primitives for Microsoft.Extensions.AI on 2026-08-13. These allow apps to route requests across multiple AI providers and fall back automatically on errors or latency thresholds — critical for building resilient, cost-optimised AI apps. Lab against a multi-model scenario using the new IChatClient routing middleware.

items.title: Explore APIM AI Gateway Tier for App Service-Hosted Agents
items.description: A 2026-08-11 Apps on Azure blog post details how the new API Management AI Gateway tier changes the architecture for App Service-hosted agents, including governed model access, MCP pass-through, token quota policies, and semantic caching. Key reading for anyone designing a governed AI API layer in front of hosted agent workloads.

items.title: Explore Serverless Agents in Azure Functions
items.description: A 2026-08-12 Apps on Azure blog post shows how to embed AI agent behaviour into existing Azure Functions-based event-driven workflows using the new Serverless Agents feature. Enables incremental AI adoption without re-platforming. Learn the trigger bindings, durable orchestration patterns, and how to wire in tool calls from a function app.
